summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of CAD s/p CABG, hypertension, anxiety, and osteoporosis presented with dysuria and urinary frequency, initially treated with nitrofurantoin which she could not tolerate due to nausea. She developed lactic acidosis in the setting of a suspected UTI and was admitted for monitoring and IV antibiotics. Urine culture confirmed E. coli, and she was treated with ceftriaxone followed by oral ciprofloxacin. Her infection resolved, lactate normalized, and she remained hemodynamically stable. Chronic anemia and thrombocytopenia were noted but stable, with outpatient follow-up planned. Due to deconditioning and gait instability, she was discharged to a short-term rehabilitation facility to complete her antibiotic course and regain strength.
